The linguistic inversion of the "Free Market."
The Classical Free Market
• Definition: A market free from
economic rent.
• Target: Landlords, Monopolists,
Predatory Creditors.
• Goal: Bring prices in line with
actual cost-value.
The Neoliberal Free Market
• Definition: A market free for
rentiers to extract wealth.
• Target: Government regulation,
taxation, public utilities.
• Goal: Maximize opportunities for
rent extraction and debt leveraging.
Classical economists sought to free markets from the parasitic overhead of hereditary
landlords and financiers. Today, neoliberal ideology has hijacked the term, using it to
deter governments from regulating the renters who are polarizing the economy.

The most powerful tool to stop debt-driven housing inflation is to tax the rental value of land. What is not paid to
the tax collector is currently left available to be paid to banks as mortgage interest. Taxing unearned rent prevents
banks from financializing housing, keeping the cost of living low and redirecting wealth back to the public.

We cannot fix a systemic crisis with marginal tweaks. Reversing the polarizing trends
of Western finance capitalism requires systemic reform: canceling unpayable debts,
taxing economic rent, and dismantling the FIRE sector's grip on global governments.
We must choose between an extractive Dark Age and a constructive future.
